q: In a pictograph of blood donations, each full blood-drop icon represents 12 units and each half icon represents 6 units. The rows show Monday 4 1/2 icons, Tuesday 3 icons, Wednesday 6 icons, and Thursday 2 1/2 icons. How many units of blood were donated over the four days?

n.0: 16 is the number of icons, not the number of units they represent.
n.1: 204 = 17 x 12 counts each half icon as a full icon.
n.3: 180 = 15 x 12 drops both half icons.

q: A line graph shows an infant's weight at monthly checkups, with the vertical axis marked every 2 pounds. Birth: on the 8-pound line. 1 month: halfway between 10 and 12. 2 months: on the 12-pound line. 3 months: halfway between 12 and 14. 4 months: on the 14-pound line. What was the mean weight gain per month from birth to 4 months?
o: 6 pounds
1.5 pounds
3 pounds
1.2 pounds
w: Total gain = 14 - 8 = 6 pounds over 4 months (birth to month 4 is 4 intervals). Mean gain = 6 / 4 = 1.5 pounds per month.

n.0: 6 pounds is the total gain over 4 months, not the gain per month.
n.2: 3 pounds is the gain in the first month only (8 to 11, the point halfway between 10 and 12).
n.3: 6 / 5 = 1.2 divides by the 5 checkups instead of the 4 one-month intervals between them.

q: A stacked bar graph shows clinic visits by age group. The April bar reaches 240 visits in total. Its 'Under 18' segment runs from 0 to 70, its '18 to 64' segment from 70 to 185, and its '65 and older' segment from 185 to 240. To the nearest tenth of a percent, what percent of April visits were by patients aged 18 to 64?
w: A middle segment's value is its top minus its bottom: 185 - 70 = 115 visits. 115 / 240 = 0.4792, or 47.9%.

n.1: 185 / 240 = 77.1% reads the top edge of the segment (185) as its value instead of subtracting the 70 below it.
n.2: 55 / 240 = 22.9% is the '65 and older' segment (240 - 185).
n.3: 70 / 240 = 29.2% is the 'Under 18' segment.

q: A patient's oral intake record for one day shows: 8 a.m. water 240 mL, 10 a.m. juice 180 mL, noon soup 360 mL, 3 p.m. tea 120 mL, 6 p.m. milk 300 mL. What percent of the day's total intake was taken before noon? Enter the number only, without the percent sign.

tr.420: the milliliters before noon, not the percent

q: A pharmacy table lists units on hand and average daily use: Drug A 180 on hand, 12 per day; Drug B 95, 8 per day; Drug C 240, 30 per day; Drug D 130, 9 per day; Drug E 210, 14 per day; Drug F 66, 5 per day. A drug is reordered when it has fewer than 14 days of supply left. Which drugs should be reordered? Select all that apply.
o: Drug C
Drug B
Drug E
Drug D
Drug A
Drug F
w: Days of supply = units on hand / daily use. A: 180 / 12 = 15. B: 95 / 8 = 11.9. C: 240 / 30 = 8. D: 130 / 9 = 14.4. E: 210 / 14 = 15. F: 66 / 5 = 13.2. Fewer than 14 days: B, C and F. Drug C has the most units on hand but the shortest supply.

n.2: 210 / 14 = 15 days; the daily use of 14 is not the number of days left.
n.3: 130 / 9 = 14.4 days, just above the 14-day threshold.
n.4: 180 / 12 = 15 days, which is not fewer than 14.

q: A double bar graph shows hospital admissions by unit in 2024 and 2025: Cardiac 320 and 368; Orthopedics 250 and 275; Pediatrics 180 and 216; Oncology 400 and 436. Which unit had the greatest percent increase in admissions from 2024 to 2025?
o: Cardiac
Oncology
Orthopedics
Pediatrics
w: Percent increase = change / 2024 value. Cardiac 48 / 320 = 15%. Orthopedics 25 / 250 = 10%. Pediatrics 36 / 180 = 20%. Oncology 36 / 400 = 9%. Pediatrics is greatest.

n.0: Cardiac had the largest increase in number (48), but 48 / 320 is only 15%.
n.1: Oncology has the tallest bars, but its 36 extra admissions are only 9% of 400.
n.2: Orthopedics rose 25 / 250 = 10%.

q: A line graph shows the number of registered nurses employed in a county: 2000, 12,000; 2005, 13,500; 2015, 15,500; 2020, 16,800. The years on the horizontal axis are plotted to scale. During which interval was the average increase per year the greatest?
w: Divide each change by the number of years. 2000 to 2005: 1,500 / 5 = 300 per year. 2005 to 2015: 2,000 / 10 = 200 per year. 2015 to 2020: 1,300 / 5 = 260 per year. 2005 to 2020: 3,300 / 15 = 220 per year. The greatest is 2000 to 2005.

n.1: This interval has the largest total increase (2,000), but it covers 10 years, so it averages 200 per year.
n.2: 1,300 over 5 years is 260 per year, less than the 300 per year from 2000 to 2005.
n.3: 3,300 over 15 years averages 220 per year.

q: A table summarizes a screening test given to 500 people. Tested positive and have the condition: 45. Tested positive and do not have the condition: 15. Tested negative and have the condition: 5. Tested negative and do not have the condition: 435. Of the people who tested positive, what percent actually have the condition? Enter the number only.

tr.12: the percent of all 500 people who tested positive
tr.90: 45 out of the 50 people who have the condition

w: 'Of the people who tested positive' sets the denominator: 45 + 15 = 60. Of these, 45 have the condition. 45 / 60 = 0.75 = 75%.

q: Maya's monthly budget of $2,400 is shown in a pie chart: Rent 35%, Food 15%, Transportation 12.5%, Savings 10%, Other 27.5%. How much more does she budget for rent than for food and transportation combined?
w: Amount = percent x total. Rent: 0.35 x 2,400 = $840. Food: 0.15 x 2,400 = $360. Transportation: 0.125 x 2,400 = $300. Food + transportation = $660. Difference: 840 - 660 = $180.

n.1: 840 - 300 = $540 compares rent with transportation only.
n.2: 840 - 360 = $480 compares rent with food only.
n.3: $660 is the food and transportation total, not how much more rent is.

q: A pie chart shows the blood types of 400 patients. Of these patients, 152 have type O blood. What is the central angle of the type O sector?
w: Fraction of the whole: 152 / 400 = 0.38. Central angle = 0.38 x 360° = 136.8°.

n.1: 38 is the percent (38%), not the angle; it must be multiplied by 360° as a decimal.
n.2: 152 is the number of patients, not degrees.
n.3: 0.62 x 360° = 223.2° is the angle for all the patients who are not type O.

q:
A stem-and-leaf plot shows the ages of patients seen at a clinic one morning (key: 3 | 1 = 31 years).
2 | 3 7 9
3 | 1 1 4 8
4 | 0 2 5 5 5 6
5 | 2 7
How many patients were older than 30 but younger than 45?
w: Ages greater than 30 and less than 45: 31, 31, 34, 38, 40, 42. That is 6 patients. The three 45s are not younger than 45.

n.0: 4 counts only the 3 stem (31, 31, 34, 38) and misses 40 and 42.
n.1: 9 includes the three patients aged 45, who are not younger than 45.
n.3: 10 counts every leaf on the 3 and 4 stems, including 45, 45, 45 and 46.

q: A histogram shows weekly study hours for a class of nursing students: 0-4 hours, 3 students; 5-9 hours, 8 students; 10-14 hours, 12 students; 15-19 hours, 5 students; 20-24 hours, 2 students. What percent of the students studied at least 10 hours? Round to the nearest tenth and enter the number only.

tr.19: the number of students, not the percent
tr.36.7: the percent who studied fewer than 10 hours

q: A histogram shows the systolic blood pressures of 50 adults: 100-109, 6 adults; 110-119, 14 adults; 120-129, 17 adults; 130-139, 9 adults; 140-149, 4 adults. Which statement must be true?
o: Over half the adults had pressures of 130 or above
Exactly 4 adults had a systolic pressure of 140
The median pressure is in the 120-129 interval
The most common single reading was 125
w: With 50 values, the median is the mean of the 25th and 26th values. Running totals: 6, then 20, then 37. The 25th and 26th values both fall in the 120-129 interval.

n.0: Only 9 + 4 = 13 of 50 adults (26%) were at 130 or above.
n.1: The 4 adults are somewhere in 140-149; a histogram does not show exact values.
n.3: The tallest bar shows the most common interval, not any single reading.

q: A dot plot shows the number of missed medication doses reported by 20 patients: 0 doses, 7 dots; 1 dose, 5 dots; 2 doses, 4 dots; 3 doses, 2 dots; 4 doses, 1 dot; 6 doses, 1 dot. What fraction of the patients missed 2 or more doses?
w: Patients with 2 or more missed doses: 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 8. 8 / 20 = 2/5.

n.0: 4 / 20 = 1/5 counts only 3 or more doses, leaving out the 4 patients who missed exactly 2.
n.2: 12 / 20 = 3/5 is the fraction who missed fewer than 2 doses.
n.3: 13 / 20 counts everyone who missed 1 or more doses.

q: A box plot of waiting times, in minutes, at a walk-in clinic shows a minimum of 4, a first quartile of 11, a median of 18, a third quartile of 27, and a maximum of 52. Which statement is supported by the plot?
o: About 25% of the patients waited over 18 minutes
About half the waits were 11 to 27 minutes
The interquartile range was 48 minutes
The mean waiting time was 18 minutes
w: The box runs from Q1 (11) to Q3 (27) and holds the middle 50% of the data, so about half the waits were between 11 and 27 minutes.

n.0: About 50% of the values lie above the median of 18, not 25%.
n.2: 52 - 4 = 48 is the range. The IQR is 27 - 11 = 16 minutes.
n.3: 18 is the median; a box plot does not show the mean.

q: In a pie chart of a clinic's annual expenses, the medical supplies sector has a central angle of 54°. Medical supplies cost $13,500 for the year. What were the clinic's total annual expenses? Enter the number of dollars only, without commas.

tr.15: the supplies percent, not the total
tr.250: 13,500 / 54, treating the angle as the percent
tr.2025: 13,500 x 0.15, applying the percent instead of dividing by it

w: Fraction of the whole: 54 / 360 = 0.15 (15%). Supplies = 0.15 x total, so total = 13,500 / 0.15 = $90,000.

q:
A stem-and-leaf plot shows hemoglobin levels, in g/dL, for 11 blood donors (key: 12 | 4 = 12.4).
11 | 2 6 8
12 | 0 4 4 9
13 | 1 5 7
14 | 3
How many donors had a hemoglobin level below 12.5 g/dL?
w: Values below 12.5: 11.2, 11.6, 11.8, 12.0, 12.4, 12.4. Each leaf is one donor, so the repeated 4 counts twice: 6 donors.

n.0: 7 includes 12.9, which is above 12.5.
n.1: 5 counts the repeated leaf 12.4 once; each leaf is a separate donor.
n.3: 3 counts only the 11 stem and misses 12.0, 12.4 and 12.4.

q: A school nurse surveys 270 students about how they get to school and plans a pie chart of the results: walk 45, bus 81, car 126, bike 18. What central angle should the bus sector have?
w: Bus fraction: 81 / 270 = 0.3. Central angle = 0.3 x 360° = 108°.

n.0: 126 / 270 x 360° = 168° is the car sector.
n.1: 81 is the number of bus riders, not degrees.
n.3: 30 is the percent (30%); as a decimal it must be multiplied by 360°.

q: A histogram shows the birth weights of 40 infants: 5.0-5.9 lb, 3 infants; 6.0-6.9 lb, 9 infants; 7.0-7.9 lb, 15 infants; 8.0-8.9 lb, 10 infants; 9.0-9.9 lb, 3 infants. Which statement is supported by the histogram?
o: More than one-third of the infants weighed 8.0 pounds or more
Fewer than 1 in 3 infants weighed under 7.0 pounds
Exactly 15 infants weighed 7.5 pounds
The heaviest infant weighed 9.9 pounds
w: Under 7.0 lb: 3 + 9 = 12 infants. 12 / 40 = 30%, which is less than 1/3 (about 33.3%).

n.0: 10 + 3 = 13 infants, and 13 / 40 = 32.5%, which is less than one-third (33.3%).
n.2: The 15 infants weighed somewhere from 7.0 to 7.9 lb; a histogram does not give single values.
n.3: The top interval shows only that the heaviest infants weighed between 9.0 and 9.9 lb.

q: A pie chart shows the preferred shifts of 600 hospital staff members: Day 38%, Evening 22%, and the rest split between Night and Rotating. The Night sector is three times as large as the Rotating sector. How many staff members prefer the night shift?
w: Remaining percent: 100 - 38 - 22 = 40%. Night is 3 parts and Rotating 1 part, so Night = 3/4 x 40% = 30%. 0.30 x 600 = 180.

n.1: 60 is the Rotating group (10% of 600).
n.2: 240 is the whole remaining 40%, Night and Rotating together.
n.3: 120 splits the remaining 40% evenly (20% each) instead of 3 to 1.

q: A scatterplot shows the hours of sleep the night before (x) and reaction time on a driving test, in milliseconds (y), for 25 adults. The points fall close to a straight line that slopes downward from left to right. Which best describes the relationship?
o: No correlation
Strong positive correlation
Weak negative correlation
Strong negative correlation
w: A downward slope from left to right means that as x increases, y tends to decrease: a negative correlation. Points close to a line make it strong.

n.0: No correlation is a cloud with no direction; these points follow a clear line.
n.1: A positive correlation rises from left to right; this pattern falls.
n.2: A weak correlation has widely scattered points; these fall close to the line.

q: A health class lists four pairs of variables that could be graphed on scatterplots. Which pair would most likely show a negative correlation?
o: Outdoor temperature and monthly heating cost
Household size and weekly grocery spending
A child's height and arm span
Hours worked and gross weekly pay
w: As outdoor temperature rises, less heating is needed, so heating cost tends to fall: one variable increases while the other decreases.

n.1: Larger households tend to spend more on groceries, a positive correlation.
n.2: Taller children tend to have longer arm spans, a positive correlation.
n.3: More hours worked brings more gross pay, a positive correlation.

q: The table lists hours of exercise per week (x) and resting heart rate in beats per minute (y) for seven adults: (1, 82), (2, 79), (3, 76), (4, 74), (5, 70), (6, 69), (7, 65). Which statement best describes the relationship shown in a scatterplot of these data?
o: Heart rate tends to fall as weekly exercise hours rise
Exercise hours tend to rise as heart rate rises
There is no correlation, since the drops are uneven
Heart rate falls by exactly 3 beats per extra hour
w: As x goes from 1 to 7, y goes from 82 to 65, so y tends to decrease as x increases: a negative correlation.

n.1: Heart rate falls as exercise rises; the two move in opposite directions, not together.
n.2: Uneven drops (3, 3, 2, 4, 1, 4) still form a steady downward trend; no correlation would show no direction at all.
n.3: The drops are 3, 3, 2, 4, 1 and 4 beats, so the decrease is not exactly 3 each hour.

q: The table lists hours studied (x) and exam score (y) for seven students: (2, 61), (3, 66), (4, 70), (5, 52), (6, 79), (7, 83), (8, 88). When the data are graphed on a scatterplot, which point does not fit the overall trend?
w: Scores rise about 4 to 5 points per extra hour, so a student who studied 5 hours would be expected to score about 74. A score of 52 sits far below the pattern.

n.0: (8, 88) is the highest point, but it continues the upward trend.
n.1: (4, 70) is about 4 points above (3, 66), in line with the trend.
n.3: (2, 61) has the lowest x-value, and its score fits the rising pattern from the left.

q: A study of 30 hospitals found a strong positive correlation between the number of parking spaces and the number of patient falls reported each year. Which conclusion is best supported by this finding?
o: Reducing parking spaces will reduce patient falls
The link is a coincidence, since parking cannot affect falls
Adding parking spaces will lead to more patient falls
Both may rise with a third factor, such as hospital size
w: Correlation does not show causation. Larger hospitals have more parking and more patients, so more falls are reported; a third variable can explain both.

n.0: This also assumes cause and effect, just in the other direction of change.
n.1: A strong correlation across 30 hospitals is a real pattern, not chance; a third variable such as hospital size explains it.
n.2: This claims parking causes falls; a correlation alone does not show cause and effect.

q: A trend line on a scatterplot of weekly study hours (x) and exam score (y) passes through the points (4, 68) and (10, 83). Using the trend line, what exam score is predicted for a student who studies 12 hours per week?
w: Slope = (83 - 68) / (10 - 4) = 15 / 6 = 2.5 points per hour. From (10, 83), 2 more hours adds 2 x 2.5 = 5, so the prediction is 88.

n.0: 83 + 2.5 adds the slope once, but 12 hours is 2 hours beyond 10.
n.2: Using 6 / 15 = 0.4 inverts the slope (run over rise), giving 83 + 0.8.
n.3: 83 / 10 x 12 = 99.6 treats the line as passing through the origin (direct variation), but it starts at 58.

q: A scatterplot of children's ages, in years (x), and heights, in inches (y), has a trend line passing through (3, 37) and (8, 50). According to the trend line, how many inches does height increase for each additional year of age? Enter your answer as a decimal.

tr.13: the total change in height, not the change per year
tr.6.25: 50 / 8, a single point's ratio instead of the change

w: Slope = change in y / change in x = (50 - 37) / (8 - 3) = 13 / 5 = 2.6 inches per year.

q: A trend line was fit to data on daily water intake and age for a sample of adults aged 20 to 60. For which age is a prediction made from the trend line least reliable?
o: 41 years
85 years
25 years
58 years
w: Predicting within the range of the data (interpolation) is reasonable. Age 85 is far outside the 20 to 60 range, so that prediction is an extrapolation and the least reliable.

n.0: 41 is near the middle of the data, where the trend line is best supported.
n.2: 25 is inside the 20 to 60 range, so it is an interpolation.
n.3: 58 is near the upper end but still inside the 20 to 60 range of the data.

q: The trend line for a scatterplot of hours since a dose (x) and drug concentration in the blood, in mcg/mL (y), is y = -1.8x + 24. According to the trend line, after how many hours will the concentration be 9 mcg/mL? Round to the nearest tenth.

tr.7.8: substituting 9 for x (24 - 16.2) instead of for y

q: A student is choosing data sets to graph on scatterplots for a class project. Which pairs of variables would most likely show a positive correlation? Select all that apply.
o: Hours of TV watched per day and test scores
Cigarettes smoked per day and lung capacity
Number of absences and final course grade
Weight of a package and its shipping cost
A person's height and arm span
Minutes spent jogging and calories burned
w: Positive correlation: both variables tend to increase together. Taller people have longer arm spans, longer jogs burn more calories, and heavier packages cost more to ship.

n.0: More TV time tends to go with lower test scores, a negative correlation.
n.1: More smoking tends to go with lower lung capacity, a negative correlation.
n.2: More absences tend to go with lower grades, a negative correlation.

q: A trend line relating certified nursing assistants' years of experience (x) to hourly wage in dollars (y) is y = 0.75x + 16.50. What does the 0.75 represent?
o: The predicted wage increase for each additional year
The predicted number of years needed to earn $16.50
The predicted hourly wage after one year of experience
The predicted starting wage for a CNA with no experience
w: In y = mx + b, the slope m is the change in y for each 1-unit increase in x. Here wages are predicted to rise $0.75 per hour for each additional year.

n.1: $16.50 is predicted at 0 years; 0.75 is a rate, not a number of years.
n.2: After one year the predicted wage is 0.75 + 16.50 = $17.25, not $0.75.
n.3: The starting wage (x = 0) is the y-intercept, $16.50.

q: A clinic's trend line for monthly advertising spending, x (in hundreds of dollars), and new patients, y, is y = 4x + 30. In March the clinic spent $1,200 on advertising and gained 70 new patients. How does March compare with the trend line's prediction?
o: 35.2 more than predicted
8 more than predicted
8 fewer than predicted
22 more than predicted
w: $1,200 is 12 hundred dollars, so x = 12. Predicted y = 4(12) + 30 = 78. Actual 70 is 78 - 70 = 8 fewer than predicted.

n.0: Using x = 1.2 (thousands) gives 4.8 + 30 = 34.8; x is in hundreds, so x = 12.
n.1: The size is right, but 70 is below 78, so March was under the prediction.
n.3: 70 - 48 = 22 uses 4 x 12 and leaves out the 30 in the equation.

q: A nurse records the pulse rates of eight patients, in beats per minute: 72, 88, 64, 90, 76, 70, 84, 68. What is the median pulse rate?
w: Order the values: 64, 68, 70, 72, 76, 84, 88, 90. With 8 values, the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (72 + 76) / 2 = 74.

n.0: 612 / 8 = 76.5 is the mean, not the median.
n.1: 76 is only one of the two middle values; with an even count, average the two.
n.3: (90 + 76) / 2 = 83 takes the middle of the list as written, without ordering it first.

q: A uniform store records the sizes of the last 10 pairs of nursing clogs it sold: 8, 9, 7.5, 9, 10, 8, 9, 11, 8.5, 9. What is the mode of the sizes sold?
w: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Size 9 appears 4 times, more than any other size.

n.0: 89 / 10 = 8.9 is the mean of the sizes.
n.1: Size 8 appears only twice, fewer times than size 9.
n.3: 4 is how many times size 9 appears, not the size itself.

q: The daily patient census on a medical unit for one week was 28, 31, 24, 35, 29, 22, and 33. What is the range of the daily census for the week?
w: Range = maximum - minimum = 35 - 22 = 13.

n.0: 33 - 28 = 5 subtracts the first value from the last as listed, not the minimum from the maximum.
n.2: 35 - 24 = 11 uses 24 as the minimum, but 22 is smaller.
n.3: 31 - 22 = 9 uses 31 as the maximum, but 35 is larger.

q: To qualify for an honors program, Jordan needs a mean score of at least 85 on five exams. Jordan's first four scores are 78, 91, 84, and 88. What is the lowest score Jordan can earn on the fifth exam and still qualify?

tr.85: the target mean, not the needed score
tr.85.25: the mean of the first four scores

w: Total needed = mean x count = 85 x 5 = 425. Current total = 78 + 91 + 84 + 88 = 341. Fifth score = 425 - 341 = 84.

q: In a nursing course, exams count for 50% of the final grade, quizzes for 30%, and homework for 20%. Priya's averages are 82 on exams, 90 on quizzes, and 95 on homework. What is Priya's final course grade? Enter the number only.
A morning section of 12 students had a mean quiz score of 75, and an afternoon section of 28 students had a mean quiz score of 85. What is the mean quiz score of all 40 students?

n.0: (12 x 85 + 28 x 75) / 40 = 78 swaps the section sizes.
n.1: The larger section pulls the mean toward 85, but the 12 lower scores still count.
n.3: (75 + 85) / 2 = 80 averages the two means, ignoring that the sections have different sizes.

q: The mean of six lab values is 40. A seventh lab value of 61 is added to the data set. What is the mean of all seven values?
w: Original total = 6 x 40 = 240. New total = 240 + 61 = 301. New mean = 301 / 7 = 43.

n.0: 301 / 6 = 50.2 divides the new total by the old count.
n.2: 40 + 21 / 6 = 43.5 spreads the extra 21 over 6 values instead of 7.
n.3: (40 + 61) / 2 = 50.5 averages the old mean with the new value as if they had equal weight.

q: A survey of 25 households records the number of children in each: 0 children, 4 households; 1 child, 7 households; 2 children, 8 households; 3 children, 4 households; 4 children, 2 households. What is the mean number of children per household? Enter your answer as a decimal.

tr.2: the median or mode, not the mean
tr.5: the mean of the household counts (25 / 5)
tr.8.6: 43 / 5, dividing by the number of categories instead of households

q: A frequency table shows quiz scores for 20 students: a score of 6, 2 students; 7, 4 students; 8, 4 students; 9, 6 students; 10, 4 students. What is the median quiz score?
w: With 20 values, the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th. Running totals: 2, 6, 10, 16, 20. The 10th value is 8 and the 11th is 9, so the median is (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5.

n.0: 166 / 20 = 8.3 is the mean, not the median.
n.1: 9 is the mode (6 students) and only the 11th value.
n.2: 8 is the middle of the score values 6 to 10 ignoring the frequencies, and it is only the 10th value.

q: A data set of wait times, in minutes, is 12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 22, 38. Which statement about the data set is true?
o: The median of the wait times is 20
The mean exceeds the median
The range of the wait times is 23
The mode of the wait times is 2
w: Mean = 140 / 7 = 20. Median = 4th value = 18. 20 > 18, so the mean is greater than the median (the 38 pulls the mean up).

n.0: 20 is the mean; the median is the middle (4th) value, 18.
n.2: 38 - 15 = 23 uses the mode as the minimum; the range is 38 - 12 = 26.
n.3: 15 appears twice; the mode is 15, not the number of times it appears.

q: The mean of 8 blood glucose readings is 115 mg/dL. When one reading is removed, the mean of the remaining 7 readings is 110 mg/dL. What was the value of the removed reading, in mg/dL?

tr.120: 115 + 5, adding the change in the mean
tr.112.5: the average of the two means

w: Total of 8 readings = 8 x 115 = 920. Total of 7 readings = 7 x 110 = 770. Removed reading = 920 - 770 = 150 mg/dL.

q: The ordered data set 3, 5, 8, 11, 14, 20 has a median of 9.5. A seventh value, 9, is added to the data set. What is the new median?
w: New ordered set: 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, 14, 20. With 7 values, the median is the 4th value, 9.

n.1: 9.5 was the median before the new value was added.
n.2: 70 / 7 = 10 is the new mean.
n.3: (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5 averages two values, but an odd count has a single middle value.

q: The wait times, in minutes, for seven patients at an urgent care center were 12, 14, 14, 16, 17, 18, and 65. Which measure best describes a typical wait time for these patients, and why?
o: The mean, because it uses every value in the data set
The median, because the 65-minute wait pulls the mean up
The range, because it shows the spread from 12 to 65
The mode, because 14 is the most common wait time
w: The mean is 156 / 7 = 22.3 minutes, higher than six of the seven waits because the outlier 65 pulls it up. The median, 16, is resistant to the outlier and describes a typical wait.

n.0: Using every value is exactly why the mean is distorted here: the 65 drags it above six of the seven waits.
n.2: The range measures spread, not a typical value, and it is inflated by the outlier.
n.3: 14 appears only twice in seven values, so it says little about the center.

q: A histogram of household incomes in a town has a tall peak on the left and a long tail stretching to the right. Which statement about the incomes is most likely true?
o: The mean and median are about equal
The distribution is skewed to the left
The mean is greater than the median
The median is greater than the mean
w: A long tail to the right is a right (positive) skew. The few very high incomes pull the mean toward the tail, so the mean is greater than the median.

n.0: Mean and median are about equal in a symmetric distribution, not a skewed one.
n.1: Skew is named for the tail, not the peak; the tail here is on the right.
n.3: That relationship fits a left-skewed distribution, where the tail is on the low side.

q: On an easy 20-point quiz, most students scored from 18 to 20 points, and a few students scored between 5 and 10 points. Which describes the shape of the score distribution and how its mean compares with its median?
o: Skewed right; the mean is greater than the median
Skewed left; the mean is greater than the median
Skewed left; the mean is less than the median
Skewed right; the mean is less than the median
w: The few low scores form a long tail on the left, so the distribution is skewed left. Those low scores pull the mean down below the median.

n.0: This names the skew by where the scores pile up (the right); skew is named for the tail, which is on the left.
n.1: The shape is right, but the low tail pulls the mean below the median, not above it.
n.3: The tail is on the left, so the distribution is skewed left, not right.

q: Two clinics both have a mean wait time of 20 minutes. The standard deviation of the wait times is 3 minutes at Clinic A and 9 minutes at Clinic B. Which statement is correct?
o: Clinic B's wait times are more spread out around 20 minutes
Clinic B's patients wait longer on average than Clinic A's
Clinic A sees more patients, so its wait times vary less
Clinic A's median wait time is greater than Clinic B's
w: Standard deviation measures spread: roughly the typical distance of values from the mean. A larger SD (9 vs 3) means Clinic B's waits vary more around the shared mean of 20.

n.1: Both clinics have the same mean of 20 minutes; SD describes spread, not the average.
n.2: SD does not depend on the number of patients; nothing in the data gives patient counts.
n.3: Standard deviation gives no information about which median is larger.

q: A data set of daily exercise minutes for seven patients is 4, 6, 7, 7, 9, 10, 41. If the value 41 is removed from the data set, how do the mean and the median change?
o: The mean falls by about 4.8; the median falls to 6.5
The mean and median both fall by about 4.8
The mean falls by about 4.8; the median stays at 7
The mean falls by about 5.9; the median stays at 7
w: Before: mean = 84 / 7 = 12, median = 7. After: 4, 6, 7, 7, 9, 10 has mean 43 / 6 = 7.17 and median (7 + 7) / 2 = 7. The mean drops by about 4.8; the median does not change.

n.0: 6.5 averages 6 and 7, but the two middle values of the six remaining are 7 and 7.
n.1: The median is resistant to the outlier: the two middle values are both 7, so it stays at 7.
n.3: 41 / 7 = 5.9 is the outlier's share of the old mean, but the new mean is computed over 6 values: 12 - 7.17 = 4.8.

q: The mean price of 10 homes sold on a street last year was $310,000. If the one home that sold for $940,000 is removed, what is the mean price of the other 9 homes, in thousands of dollars? Enter the number only.

tr.310: the original mean, before the outlier is removed

w: Total of 10 homes = 10 x 310 = 3,100 thousand. Remove 940: 3,100 - 940 = 2,160 thousand. Mean of 9 = 2,160 / 9 = 240 thousand dollars.

q: Each of the 15 employees at a pharmacy receives a raise of $2.00 per hour. Before the raise, the hourly wages had a mean of $18.40, a median of $17.75, and a range of $9.50. Which describes the wages after the raise?
o: Mean $20.40, median $19.75, range $11.50
Mean $20.40, median $19.75, range $9.50
Mean $18.53, median $19.75, range $9.50
Mean $20.40, median $17.75, range $9.50
w: Adding the same amount to every value adds it to the mean and the median, but the gap between the highest and lowest wage does not change. Mean 18.40 + 2 = 20.40; median 17.75 + 2 = 19.75; range stays 9.50.

n.0: The range does not change: the highest and lowest wages both rise by $2.
n.2: Each employee gets $2, so the mean rises by $2, not by 2 / 15.
n.3: The middle wage also rises by $2, so the median becomes $19.75.

q: The annual salaries, in thousands of dollars, of the seven employees at a small clinic are 42, 45, 45, 48, 51, 54, and 160. How much greater is the mean salary than the median salary, in thousands of dollars? Round to the nearest tenth.

tr.18.6: mean minus the mode (45) instead of the median

w: Sum = 445, so mean = 445 / 7 = 63.57. Median = 4th value = 48. Difference = 63.57 - 48 = 15.57, about 15.6 thousand dollars.

q: In a data set of 20 hospital stays, the longest stay, 9 days, is entered by mistake as 90 days. Which statistic stays the same despite the error?
o: The range
The standard deviation
The median
The mean
w: The median depends on the middle values (the 10th and 11th of 20). Changing the largest value does not move the middle, so the median is unchanged.

n.0: The maximum changes from 9 to 90, so the range grows by 81.
n.1: The new extreme value lies far from the mean, which increases the spread.
n.3: The total rises by 81, so the mean rises by 81 / 20 = 4.05 days.

q: A large set of adult cholesterol levels is roughly symmetric and bell-shaped, with a mean of 190 mg/dL and a standard deviation of 20 mg/dL. Which statement is best supported?
o: About 68% of the levels fall between 170 and 210 mg/dL
About 95% of the levels fall between 170 and 210 mg/dL
About half of the levels are above 210 mg/dL
About 68% of the levels fall between 150 and 230 mg/dL
w: In a bell-shaped distribution, about 68% of values fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean: 190 - 20 = 170 to 190 + 20 = 210.

n.1: 170 to 210 is within 1 standard deviation, which holds about 68%, not 95%.
n.2: About half are above the mean of 190; only about 16% are above 210.
n.3: 150 to 230 is within 2 standard deviations, which holds about 95%, not 68%.

q: A clinic records each new patient's blood type (A, B, AB, or O) to help plan its blood supply. Which measure of center can be used to describe these data?
o: The median
The weighted mean
The mode
The mean
w: Blood type is categorical data with no numeric values or natural order, so the mode (the most common type) is the only usable measure of center.

n.0: A median needs values that can be put in a meaningful order; A, B, AB and O have none.
n.1: A weighted mean also needs numeric values to multiply by the weights.
n.3: A mean needs numeric values to add, and blood types are categories.

q: Data set A is 14, 18, 22, 26, 30. Data set B is 8, 21, 22, 23, 36. Which statement correctly compares the two data sets?
o: Same mean and median, but B has the greater range
Same mean and range, but the medians differ
Same mean and median, but A has the greater range
Same median, but B has the greater mean and range
w: A: sum 110, mean 22, median 22, range 30 - 14 = 16. B: sum 110, mean 22, median 22, range 36 - 8 = 28. Same center, but B is more spread out.

n.1: Both medians are 22 (the 3rd value of 5), and the ranges are 16 and 28, not equal.
n.2: A's evenly spaced values span only 30 - 14 = 16, while B's span 36 - 8 = 28.
n.3: B's values also sum to 110, so both means are 22; only the ranges differ (16 and 28).

q: A nurse researcher studies whether patients' fasting blood glucose levels are affected by the number of steps they walk each day. Every patient wears the same model of step counter for 30 days, and glucose is always checked at 7 a.m. Which is the dependent variable?
o: Fasting blood glucose level
Number of steps walked each day
Time of day glucose is checked
Model of step counter worn
w: The dependent variable is the measured outcome that may respond to the change. The study asks whether glucose is affected by daily steps, so fasting glucose level depends on the number of steps walked.

n.1: Daily steps is the independent variable: it is the factor whose effect on glucose is being tested, even though it is named second.
n.2: Checking glucose at 7 a.m. for every patient holds this factor constant, which makes it a controlled variable.
n.3: Every patient wears the same model, so it is held constant: a controlled variable, not the measured outcome.

q: A taxi company sets the cost of a ride, C, based on the number of miles driven, m. Which statement correctly identifies the variables in this relationship?
o: C is independent, because it is the amount the rider pays
m is independent, and C depends on m
m is dependent, because it is measured during the ride
Both are dependent, because each changes with the other
w: The cost is calculated from the miles, so miles (m) is the input, or independent variable, and cost (C) is the output, or dependent variable.

n.0: The amount paid is the result of the miles driven, which makes C dependent.
n.2: Being measured does not make a variable dependent; m is the input that sets the cost.
n.3: One variable is the input and the other the output; C changes because m changes, not the reverse.

q: A study asks whether a person's resting heart rate is affected by the number of cups of coffee the person drinks per day. What is the independent variable in this study?
o: Time of day heart rate is measured
Resting heart rate
Cups of coffee per day
The people in the study
w: The study tests the effect of coffee intake on heart rate. Coffee intake is the possible cause (independent); heart rate is the response (dependent).

n.0: Measurement time should be held the same, which makes it a controlled variable.
n.1: Heart rate is named first, but it is the outcome being affected, so it is dependent.
n.3: The participants are the sample, not a variable.

q: A researcher graphs how the dose of a pain reliever, in milligrams, affects the time until a patient reports relief, in minutes. How should the axes of the graph be labeled?
o: Dose on the y-axis, because the dose is what the researcher controls
Time until relief on the x-axis, because time is the independent variable
Either variable on either axis, since the graph shows a correlation
Dose on the x-axis and time until relief on the y-axis
w: The independent variable (dose, which the researcher sets) goes on the x-axis, and the dependent variable (time until relief, which responds) goes on the y-axis.

n.0: The variable the researcher controls is independent and belongs on the x-axis, not the y-axis.
n.1: Time is often independent, but here the time until relief is the response to the dose, so it is dependent.
n.2: Convention places the independent variable on the x-axis so the graph shows how y responds to x.

q: Students test how water temperature affects the time it takes 5 grams of sugar to dissolve. They use the same cup, the same volume of water, and the same stirring speed in every trial. What is the stirring speed in this investigation?
o: The dependent variable
The independent variable
A controlled variable
The control group
w: Stirring speed is kept the same in every trial so it cannot affect the results. A factor held constant is a controlled variable.

n.0: The dependent variable is the outcome measured: time to dissolve.
n.1: The independent variable is the factor deliberately changed: water temperature.
n.3: A control group is a set of trials used for comparison, not a factor held constant.

q: A table lists the number of hours since a medication was given and the amount of the medication remaining in the bloodstream, in milligrams. Which statement correctly describes the variables?
o: The amount remaining depends on the hours since the dose
The hours since the dose depend on the amount remaining
The amount remaining is independent, since it is the value measured
Both are independent, since neither is set by the nurse
w: Time passes on its own, and the amount remaining changes as time passes. Time is independent and the amount remaining is dependent.

n.1: This reverses the relationship; elapsed time does not change because of the amount in the blood.
n.2: A measured outcome is the dependent variable, not the independent one.
n.3: A variable can be independent without anyone setting it; elapsed time is the input here.

q: A gym's total membership cost, y, in dollars, after x months is given by y = 12x + 30. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the variables?
o: x is independent; each increase of 1 in x raises y by 12
x is independent; each increase of 1 in x raises y by 30
y is independent; each increase of 1 in y raises x by 12
x is dependent, because it is multiplied by 12
w: The cost is calculated from the number of months, so x is independent and y is dependent. The coefficient 12 is the change in y for each 1-unit increase in x ($12 per month); 30 is the starting fee.

n.1: 30 is the starting value (the y-intercept), not the change per month.
n.2: This swaps the roles of the variables; y is calculated from x.
n.3: Having a coefficient does not make a variable dependent; x is the input.

q: A graph has 'Outdoor temperature (°F)' labeled on the x-axis and 'Heat-related emergency room visits' labeled on the y-axis. Which question is the graph designed to investigate?
o: How does outdoor temperature affect emergency room visits?
How do emergency room visits change from month to month?
How do emergency room visits affect outdoor temperature?
How many patients visit the emergency room each day?
w: The x-axis holds the independent variable and the y-axis the dependent variable, so the graph shows how ER visits respond to temperature.

n.1: Change over months would need time on the x-axis, but the x-axis shows temperature.
n.2: This reverses the variables; the y-axis variable is the one that responds.
n.3: A daily count needs no temperature axis; this graph relates two variables.

q: A dietitian studies whether daily sodium intake affects blood pressure. All participants are 40 to 50 years old, follow the same exercise routine, and take no blood pressure medication. Which are controlled variables in this study? Select all that apply.
o: Blood pressure
Exercise routine
Daily sodium intake
Age range of participants
Medication use
w: Controlled variables are factors held the same for everyone so they cannot explain differences in the outcome: the age range, the exercise routine, and medication use.

n.0: Blood pressure is the outcome measured, so it is the dependent variable.
n.2: Sodium intake is the factor being tested, so it is the independent variable.

q: A table shows the number of workers assigned to a job (x) and the days needed to finish it (y): 2 workers, 12 days; 4 workers, 6 days; 6 workers, 4 days; 8 workers, 3 days. Which statement correctly describes the variables?
o: Workers depends on days needed; as days decrease, workers decrease
Days needed depends on workers; as workers increase, days increase
Days needed depends on workers; as workers increase, days decrease
Neither depends on the other, since y falls as x rises
w: The number of workers is the input (independent) and the days needed is the output (dependent). From 2 to 8 workers, the days fall from 12 to 3.

n.0: This reverses the roles, and in the table fewer days go with more workers, not fewer.
n.1: The roles are right, but the days fall as workers increase.
n.3: A falling y as x rises is still a relationship (an inverse one), not a lack of one.

q: A student writes each pair of variables in the form (independent variable, dependent variable). Which pair is written in the correct order?
o: (Hours worked at $18 per hour, weekly paycheck)
(Weekly grocery bill, number of people in the household)
(Distance traveled, hours driven at a steady speed)
(Crop yield, inches of rainfall)
w: The paycheck is calculated from the hours worked, so hours worked is independent and the paycheck is dependent; the pair is in the correct order.

n.1: The grocery bill depends on household size, so the order is reversed.
n.2: At a steady speed, distance depends on the hours driven, so the order is reversed.
n.3: Crop yield depends on rainfall, so the order is reversed.

q: A child's dose of a liquid medicine, M, in milliliters, is calculated from the child's weight, W, in kilograms, using the formula M = 0.4W. Which statement is correct?
o: M is independent, because the dose is what the nurse controls
M is independent, and W rises by 2 kg when M rises by 5 mL
W is independent, and M rises by 12.5 mL when W rises by 5 kg
W is independent, and M rises by 2 mL when W rises by 5 kg
w: The dose is calculated from the weight, so W is independent and M is dependent. An increase of 5 kg changes M by 0.4 x 5 = 2 mL.

n.0: The dose is the output of the formula; the weight is the input.
n.1: This swaps the variables; the dose is calculated from the weight.
n.2: 5 / 0.4 = 12.5 divides by the rate instead of multiplying: 0.4 x 5 = 2 mL.

q: A math teacher lists four everyday situations involving two related quantities. Which situation is an example of direct variation?
o: The balance on a $500 gift card after spending $25 per week
The time needed to drive 100 miles at different speeds
Total pay at $22 per hour, with no other pay
A taxi fare of $3 for pickup plus $2.50 per mile
w: Direct variation has the form y = kx: zero hours gives zero pay, and doubling the hours doubles the pay (pay = 22h).

n.0: Balance = 500 - 25w is a decreasing linear relationship, not y = kx.
n.1: Time = 100 / speed is inverse variation: doubling the speed halves the time.
n.3: Fare = 2.50m + 3 is linear, but the $3 starting fee means it does not pass through the origin, so it is not direct variation.

q: Four tables each use the x-values 1, 2, 3, 4. Which set of y-values shows a linear relationship between x and y?
w: A relationship is linear when equal steps in x give equal differences in y. Here y rises by 3 each time (5, 8, 11, 14).

n.0: The differences are 2, 4, 6, which are not constant.
n.1: These are the squares of x; the differences are 3, 5, 7.
n.3: Each y doubles (a constant ratio), which is exponential; the differences are 2, 4, 8.

q: A home health agency charges C dollars for a visit lasting h hours, where C = 45h + 30. In this equation, what does the 30 represent?
o: The number of hours covered by the base fee
The total cost of a 1-hour visit
The cost for each hour of the visit
A flat $30 fee on top of the hourly charge
w: In C = 45h + 30, the constant 30 is the y-intercept: the cost when h = 0. It is a fixed fee added to the $45 per hour.

n.0: 30 is in dollars, not hours, and the equation includes no free hours.
n.1: A 1-hour visit costs 45(1) + 30 = $75.
n.2: The cost per hour is the slope, 45.

q: A table shows the x-values 2, 5, and 8 paired with the y-values 7, 17.5, and 28. Which equation models the relationship shown in the table?
o: y = x + 5

n.0: This fits (2, 7) but gives 16, not 17.5, when x = 5.
n.2: This fits (2, 7) but gives 10, not 17.5, when x = 5.
n.3: This fits (2, 7) but gives 2.8 when x = 5; y increases as x increases, so it is not inverse.

q: It takes 6 nurses 8 hours to complete a set of patient assessments. Working at the same rate, how many hours would it take 4 nurses to complete the same set of assessments?
o: 10 hours
12 hours
About 5.3 hours
6 hours
w: Fewer workers need more time: an inverse relationship with a constant product. 6 x 8 = 48 nurse-hours. 48 / 4 = 12 hours.

n.0: Adding 1 hour per missing nurse is not supported; the total work, 48 nurse-hours, must be shared.
n.2: 8 x 4 / 6 = 5.3 treats the relationship as direct, as if fewer nurses would finish sooner.
n.3: Fewer nurses cannot finish sooner; subtracting 2 hours reverses the relationship.

q: A table shows the x-values 2, 4, 5, and 10 paired with the y-values 25, 12.5, 10, and 5. Which describes the relationship between x and y?
o: Linear: y = -6.25x + 37.5
Direct variation: y = 12.5x
Inverse variation: y = 25/x
Inverse variation: y = 50/x
w: Each product xy is 50 (2 x 25, 4 x 12.5, 5 x 10, 10 x 5), so y varies inversely with x: y = 50/x.

n.0: This line fits the first two points but gives 6.25, not 10, when x = 5.
n.1: y = 12.5x fits (2, 25) but gives 50 when x = 4; also y falls as x rises.
n.2: 25 is the first y-value, not the constant; 25 / 4 = 6.25, not 12.5.

q: A table shows the volume remaining in a patient's IV bag: 0 minutes, 1,000 mL; 30 minutes, 940 mL; 60 minutes, 880 mL; 90 minutes, 820 mL. If this constant rate continues, how many minutes after the start will the bag hold 400 mL?

tr.200: 400 / 2, the time to empty the last 400 mL
tr.210: the time after the 90-minute reading (420 / 2), not after the start
tr.500: 1,000 / 2, the time to empty the full bag

w: Rate of change = (940 - 1,000) / 30 = -2 mL per minute. To fall from 1,000 to 400 mL is 600 mL, which takes 600 / 2 = 300 minutes.

q: The dose of a medicine varies directly with a patient's body weight. A patient who weighs 60 kg receives 150 mg. What dose, in milligrams, should a patient who weighs 84 kg receive?

tr.107.1: treating it as inverse variation (150 x 60 / 84)
tr.2.5: the constant of variation, not the dose

w: Direct variation: dose = k x weight. k = 150 / 60 = 2.5 mg per kg. Dose = 2.5 x 84 = 210 mg.

q: A gym charges a one-time sign-up fee plus a fixed monthly fee. A 3-month membership costs $135 in total, and an 8-month membership costs $285 in total. What is the sign-up fee?

n.0: 135 / 3 - 30 = 15 spreads the sign-up fee across the 3 months before subtracting.
n.2: 135 - 30 = 105 removes one month's fee instead of three.
n.3: $30 is the monthly fee (the slope), not the starting fee.

q: The number of doses, D, remaining in a multi-dose vial after t days of use is given by D = 40 - 3t. Which statement describes this relationship?
o: The vial starts with 40 doses and loses 3 doses per day
The vial starts with 3 doses and loses 40 doses per day
The vial starts with 40 doses and gains 3 doses per day
The vial starts with 37 doses and loses 3 doses per day
w: At t = 0, D = 40, the starting amount (y-intercept). The slope is -3, so D decreases by 3 for each day.

n.1: This swaps the intercept and the rate.
n.2: The coefficient of t is -3, a decrease, not a gain.
n.3: 37 is the amount left after 1 day; at t = 0 the vial holds 40.

q: Four tables each list three (x, y) pairs. In which table does y vary directly with x?
w: Direct variation needs the same ratio y / x for every pair: 6 / 4 = 1.5, 9 / 6 = 1.5, 15 / 10 = 1.5. So y = 1.5x.

n.0: Each product xy is 36, which is inverse variation.
n.1: The ratio is 1.5 for the first two pairs but 9 / 8 = 1.125 for the third.
n.2: y rises 2 per unit of x, but y = 2x + 5 has a starting value of 5, so the ratios (7, 4.5, 3.25) differ.

q: A solution is warmed at a constant rate. Its temperature is 26°C after 4 minutes and 44°C after 10 minutes. What was the temperature of the solution at 0 minutes?
w: Rate = (44 - 26) / (10 - 4) = 18 / 6 = 3°C per minute. Going back 4 minutes from 26°C: 26 - 4(3) = 14°C.

n.0: 26 - 18 = 8 subtracts the whole 6-minute change instead of 4 minutes' worth.
n.2: 3°C is the rate of change per minute, not the starting temperature.
n.3: 26 / 4 = 6.5 assumes direct variation (starting at 0°C), but the solution did not start at 0°C.

q: A nurse wants to display how a patient's body weight changed over 12 weekly clinic visits so that the trend is easy to see. Which type of display is most appropriate?
o: Line graph
Circle graph
Histogram
Stem-and-leaf plot
w: A line graph shows how one quantity changes over time; connecting the weekly points makes the trend visible.

n.1: A circle graph shows parts of a whole, and the weekly weights are not parts of a total.
n.2: A histogram groups values into intervals and loses the order in time.
n.3: A stem-and-leaf plot shows the spread of values but not their order over the 12 weeks.

q: A bar graph compares patient satisfaction at two clinics: Clinic A 84% and Clinic B 88%. The vertical axis starts at 82%, so Clinic B's bar appears three times as tall as Clinic A's. Which statement most accurately describes the data?
o: B's rating is about 200% higher than A's
B's rating is about 3 times A's, as the bar heights show
The difference cannot be found, since the axis does not start at 0
B's rating is 4 percentage points higher than A's
w: Read the values, not the bar heights: 88% - 84% = 4 percentage points. The axis starting at 82% makes the bars 2 and 6 units tall, which exaggerates the gap.

n.0: Bar heights of 2 and 6 would suggest a 200% increase, but the actual values differ by 4 points (about 4.8%).
n.1: The bars look 3 times as tall only because the axis is truncated; 88% is not 3 times 84%.
n.2: The values can still be read from the scale; a truncated axis distorts the picture, not the numbers.

q: A pie chart in a hospital newsletter shows how staff members answered a survey question: Yes 45%, No 38%, Unsure 27%. What is the main problem with this chart?
o: The sectors must be ordered from largest to smallest first
Three categories are too few, so a histogram is needed instead
The Unsure sector should be drawn smaller as a non-answer
The sectors total 110%, so they cannot form a single whole
w: The sectors of a pie chart must total 100% of one whole. 45 + 38 + 27 = 110%, so the chart cannot be correct; respondents may have been allowed more than one answer.

n.0: Ordering sectors can help readability, but it does not fix percents that total 110%.
n.1: A pie chart can show three categories, and a histogram is for numeric intervals, not answer categories.
n.2: Each sector's size must match its percent; shrinking one would distort the data further.

q: A health department wants to show the distribution of cholesterol levels for 200 adults, grouped into intervals of 20 mg/dL, so that readers can see where most levels fall. Which display is most appropriate?
o: Line graph
Circle graph
Scatterplot
Histogram
w: A histogram shows the distribution of one numeric variable grouped into intervals, with bar heights giving the frequency in each interval.

n.0: A line graph shows change over time, and these data have no time order.
n.1: A circle graph shows parts of a whole and makes the shape of a distribution hard to see.
n.2: A scatterplot needs two numeric variables, but only cholesterol level is given.

q: An advertisement compares a clinic's flu vaccination rate in 2020 and 2025. The rate doubled, so the artist drew the 2025 syringe picture twice as tall and twice as wide as the 2020 picture. Why is the graphic misleading?
o: The 2025 picture is twice as wide, so it understates the increase
The 2025 picture has 2 times the area, which shows the doubling accurately
The 2025 picture has 8 times the area, suggesting an eightfold increase
The 2025 picture has 4 times the area, so the increase looks larger than double
w: Scaling both dimensions by 2 multiplies the area by 2 x 2 = 4. Readers judge pictures by area, so a doubling looks like a fourfold increase.

n.0: The extra width makes the increase look larger, not smaller.
n.1: Doubling the height and the width multiplies the area by 4, not 2.
n.2: A factor of 8 (2 x 2 x 2) applies to volume; a flat picture scales its area by 4.

q: A bar graph of hospital admissions has a vertical axis that starts at 900. The 2024 bar shows 950 admissions and the 2025 bar shows 1,100 admissions, so the 2025 bar looks 4 times as tall. By what percent did admissions actually increase from 2024 to 2025? Round to the nearest tenth and enter the number only.

tr.150: the number of extra admissions, not the percent
tr.300: the visual increase in bar height (50 to 200)

w: Percent increase = (new - original) / original x 100 = (1,100 - 950) / 950 x 100 = 150 / 950 x 100 = 15.79%, about 15.8%. The truncated axis makes the bars 50 and 200 units tall, which suggests a 300% increase.

q: A researcher has recorded each of 40 adults' average daily calorie intake and their change in weight over one month. Which display best shows whether the two variables are related?
o: Line graph
Scatterplot
Double bar graph
Circle graph
w: A scatterplot plots one point per adult using two numeric variables, which shows whether they tend to rise or fall together.

n.0: A line graph tracks change over time, but these data pair two measurements for each person.
n.2: A double bar graph compares two series across categories, and 40 individual adults are not categories to compare.
n.3: A circle graph shows parts of a whole, not a relationship between two variables.

q: A news article claims 'Emergency room waits have soared' and shows a line graph covering only March and April, when the mean wait rose from 42 to 51 minutes. Over the full year, monthly mean waits ranged from 42 to 60 minutes and averaged 52 minutes. What is the best criticism of the graph?
o: The two-month window hides that April was below the yearly average
The increase from 42 to 51 minutes is a 9% rise, not a large one
The yearly average of 52 minutes proves that waits are falling
A line graph cannot show monthly changes, so a pie chart was needed
w: Choosing a short time window (cherry-picking) can make an ordinary change look dramatic. April's 51 minutes was below the yearly average of 52 and well under the 60-minute high.

n.1: The rise is 9 minutes, which is 9 / 42 = 21.4%, not 9%.
n.2: An average does not show a direction of change, so it cannot prove waits are falling.
n.3: A line graph is the right display for change over time; the problem is the window chosen.

q: A news graph titled 'ER Visits Explode' shows yearly visits at one hospital. The vertical axis runs from 4,000 to 4,600, and the years 2019, 2021, and 2024 are spaced equally along the horizontal axis. Which features make the graph misleading? Select all that apply.
o: The vertical axis begins at 4,000 instead of 0
The title states a conclusion the data may not support
The years are evenly spaced despite unequal gaps
The vertical axis is labeled with the number of visits
A line is used to show change over time
w: A truncated vertical axis exaggerates changes, equal spacing for unequal gaps (2 years, then 3 years) distorts the rate of change, and a loaded title pushes a conclusion before the reader checks the scale.

n.3: Labeling the axis with what is counted is good practice and helps readers.
n.4: A line graph is the appropriate display for change over time.

q: A hospital wants to show what percent of its $2.4 million annual budget goes to each of its five departments. Which display is most appropriate?
o: Histogram
Scatterplot
Circle graph
Line graph
w: A circle (pie) graph shows how a whole, here the total budget, is divided into parts, with each sector's size matching its percent.

n.0: A histogram shows the distribution of a numeric variable in intervals, not shares of a total.
n.1: A scatterplot shows the relationship between two numeric variables.

q: Two bar graphs are placed side by side. Hospital X's graph has a vertical axis from 0 to 50 and shows 40 infections. Hospital Y's graph has a vertical axis from 0 to 500 and shows 400 infections. Both bars reach 80% of the way up their axes. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Hospital Y had 10 times as many infections as Hospital X
The hospitals had about the same number of infections
Hospital X had 10 times as many infections as Hospital Y
Hospital Y had 80% more infections than Hospital X
w: Read each bar against its own scale: X = 40 and Y = 400. 400 / 40 = 10, so Y had 10 times as many, even though the bars look equal.

n.1: The bars look equal only because the two graphs use different scales.
n.2: This reverses the comparison; Y's value, 400, is the larger one.
n.3: 80% is how far each bar reaches up its own axis, not a comparison between the hospitals.

q: A graph of the total (cumulative) number of flu cases at a college shows 120 cases by the end of week 1, 210 by week 2, 270 by week 3, and 300 by week 4. A student says the graph shows the outbreak getting worse each week. Which statement about new cases per week is correct?
o: New cases fell each week, from 120 to 30
New cases stayed steady at about 75 per week
New cases rose each week, from 120 to 300
New cases peaked in week 4 at 300 cases
w: New cases each week are the differences between totals: 120, 210 - 120 = 90, 270 - 210 = 60, 300 - 270 = 30. A cumulative graph keeps rising even as new cases fall.

n.1: 300 / 4 = 75 is the mean per week; the actual weekly counts fell from 120 to 30.
n.2: 120 to 300 are running totals, not new cases each week.
n.3: 300 is the total after 4 weeks; only 30 of those cases were new in week 4.
